slides.say: Omar, Priya and Sam each work at a constant rate. Together they complete a job in nine hours. Omar and Priya together complete it in eighteen hours. What fraction of the job does Sam complete in one hour?
at: Omar, Priya and Sam each work

slides.say: So they ask for Sam's rate, the part of the job he does in one hour.
at: So they ask for Sam's rate

slides.say: We'll solve it in three different ways. This time there are three workers, and that's what makes it hard. So I want to use this question to show you a trick that turns three workers into two.
Omar and Priya together do one job in eighteen hours. Do we care how they split the work? Not really.
at: Omar and Priya together do one job

slides: Maybe they share it equally. Maybe Priya sits with a coffee, and Omar does everything. Together they still do one job in eighteen hours.

slides.say: So they're like one worker. Let's give them one name, Omarpriya. Now it's a normal question with two workers, Omarpriya and Sam.

slides: This works whenever a question gives the time of two workers together. We treat the two as one worker, with one rate.

slides.say: Now the math way, with equal times, like in the lesson. All three do one job in nine hours.
at: All three do one job in nine hours

slides.say: Omarpriya does one job in eighteen hours.
at: Omarpriya does one job in eighteen

slides.say: The times are different. Nine to eighteen is times two. So in eighteen hours, all three do two jobs.
Omarpriya does one of the two jobs. So Sam does the other one. Two minus one is one job in eighteen hours.
at: Two minus one is one job

slides.say: So in one hour, Sam does one eighteenth of the job.
[pause] Now the insight. We start again from the givens. All three work for nine hours, and finish the job.
Omarpriya needs eighteen hours for a whole job. Nine hours is half of that. So in nine hours, Omarpriya does half the job.
at: So in nine hours, Omarpriya does half

slides.say: So Sam does the other half, in the same nine hours.
at: So Sam does the other half

slides.say: Half a job in nine hours means a whole job in eighteen hours. So Sam alone is as fast as Omar and Priya together. And his rate is one eighteenth.
at: a whole job in eighteen hours

slides.say: [pause] And the math way with rates. We start again from the givens. All three together do a ninth of the job an hour. Omarpriya does an eighteenth.
Sam's rate is what's left. A ninth minus an eighteenth. A ninth is two eighteenths. So two eighteenths minus one eighteenth.
That's one eighteenth of the job an hour.
at: That's one eighteenth of the job

slides.say: Choice number three is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number three is our answer
